title: Filtering and sorting
summary: WHERE picks rows, ORDER BY sorts them, LIMIT keeps the top few.

steps.title: WHERE picks rows
body: `WHERE` keeps only the rows for which a condition is true:
Text goes in **single quotes**: `WHERE genre = 'Mystery'`. Double quotes are for column names with odd characters, not for text.

steps.title: Combining conditions
body: WHERE genre = 'Fantasy' AND price < 13        -- both must hold
WHERE genre = 'Fantasy' OR genre = 'Sci-Fi'   -- either may hold
WHERE genre IN ('Fantasy', 'Sci-Fi')          -- same thing, shorter
WHERE pages BETWEEN 200 AND 300               -- inclusive at both ends
WHERE title LIKE 'The %'                      -- % = any text, _ = one character
**AND binds tighter than OR**, just as `*` binds tighter than `+`. When you mix them, use parentheses so the query says what you mean:
> **Tip:** In SQLite, `LIKE` ignores case for English letters. PostgreSQL's `LIKE` is case-sensitive; it has `ILIKE` for the case-insensitive version.

code: WHERE genre = 'Fantasy' OR genre = 'Sci-Fi' AND price < 14;
options: Every Fantasy book, plus Sci-Fi books under 14
Fantasy and Sci-Fi books, all under 14
Nothing: you cannot mix AND and OR
steps.explain: `AND` is evaluated first, so it reads `Fantasy OR (Sci-Fi AND price < 14)`. Add parentheses if you meant the other thing.

steps.title: ORDER BY and LIMIT
body: ORDER BY price DESC, title   -- most expensive first; ties broken by title
- `ASC` (the default) is smallest first, `DESC` is largest first.
- Several sort keys: the second only matters when the first ties.
- `LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3` skips three rows, then takes three: the second page.
SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;
SELECT TOP 3 title FROM books ORDER BY price DESC;
SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY price DESC FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY;

sqlflow.note: SQLite sorts NULL as the smallest value, so the unpriced book sinks to the bottom of a DESC sort. PostgreSQL does the opposite (NULLs first in DESC); say `NULLS LAST` when it matters.
